closed_subgap.completed: Concrete fixed decoded-value checker, an explicitly separate eighth finding, inherited seven-finding preservation, and proved checker/gate composition.
closed_subgap.strongest_theorem: For every modeled VerificationPolicy, inherited VerificationReport, and DecodedAttributionView, evaluateEight(policy, collectReport(base, view)) = true iff Accepts(policy, base) AND FixedAttribution(view).
closed_subgap.why_substantive: Attribution is computed from exact source identifiers and aliases, people names and labels, the two-entry person-to-alias map, and the note. It is not a freely assumed eighth pass flag.
closed_subgap.precise_domain: Typed decoded strings and lists only; personToAlias is represented as a two-member association list allowing both member orders, while source and people array order remain fixed.
closed_subgap.nonvacuity: The exact fixedView satisfies the predicate and is accepted by the decoded checker.
closed_subgap.rejection_properties: Reversed sources, reversed people, and any note different from the pinned Appendix F literal are rejected regardless of the other decoded fields.
closed_subgap.provenance_limit: No proof that actual raw JSON is parsed or projected into this representation; no evidence locators, target identifiers, observation times or result reasons are added to this bounded finding-only model.

fixed_literals.note_policy: Only the documented fixed Appendix F note is admitted. Independently approved versioned replacements are outside this new fixed-profile model.

explicit_theorem_premises: Main correspondence quantifies arbitrary inherited seven-field modeled reports; it does not prove their findings true of an actual target.
Reversal rejection lemmas assume the corresponding decoded list equals the documented reverse.
Unapproved-note rejection assumes decoded note differs from the literal.
Invalid-attribution rejection assumes the independently defined FixedAttribution predicate does not hold.
proof_execution.trusted_checking_base: Pinned native Lean 4.22.0 and its standard library; no claim that the compiler or String/List equality implementation has itself been verified here.
